sources.entry: Kopia | Fast, encrypted, deduplicated backups with a web UI

summary.one_liner: Kopia is an open-source backup and restore tool that creates encrypted, compressed, deduplicated snapshots of selected files and folders and stores them in cloud, network, or local storage.
summary.what_it_does: Kopia backs up user-chosen files and directories rather than whole-machine images. Snapshots are encrypted end-to-end, compressed, and deduplicated, and the README also mentions error correction. Storage targets named in the README include Amazon S3 and S3-compatible storage, Azure Blob Storage, Backblaze B2, Google Cloud Storage, WebDAV, SFTP, local disks or NAS, and some providers via Rclone (Dropbox, OneDrive, and Google Drive were tested). A Kopia Repository Server can also host repositories on your own server. Multiple machines can back up to the same storage location. It ships both a command-line interface and a graphical user interface.
use_cases: encrypted file backups to cloud storage
backing up important folders on a personal computer
offsite backup to S3 or Backblaze B2
backing up multiple machines to one repository
backup to NAS or SFTP server
how_to_run: Download and install Kopia from the installation page linked in the README (no commands given in the README).
stack: Go (implied by CLI/GUI tooling; not named in README)
notable: End-to-end user-controlled encryption with compression, deduplication, and error correction
Works with many storage backends including S3-compatible, WebDAV, SFTP, and Rclone-managed providers
Repository Server option for self-hosting a shared backup target
caveats: Rclone support is labeled experimental; not all Rclone-supported providers have been tested
Storage costs must be provisioned and paid for by the user with the chosen provider
Backs up selected files and directories, not full machine images
